name: James
overview: James, a male from the tribe of Judah, is identified as the "brother" of Jesus and son of Mary, with "brother" understood in the sense of sharing the same womb. This familial connection grounds his significance within the immediate family of Jesus as recorded in Matthew 13:55. His identity is closely tied to his relationship with Jesus and his Jewish heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name James means "follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel," reflecting a proper name given apart from divine naming. He is also known by the title "James the Less," meaning "Jacob the younger," which distinguishes him among others with the same name as noted in Mark 15:40.
familyAndRelationships: James is explicitly described as a brother of Jesus, indicating a close family bond, and is inferred to be the son of Mary. Scripture does not provide additional family relationships beyond these, focusing primarily on his connection to Jesus and Mary as recorded in Matthew 13:55.
scriptureSignificance: James is significant as a prominent figure who initially did not believe in Jesus during His earthly ministry but came to faith after the resurrection. He emerged as a leading figure in the early Jerusalem church, presiding over key decisions such as the Jerusalem Council. His devotion to prayer and leadership are complemented by his authorship of an epistle emphasizing that genuine faith naturally produces good works, balancing Pauline teachings on faith. Tradition holds that he was martyred, underscoring his faithful witness.
